mike: Heads up — noticed a regression on canary after the kernel-selector tweak. Decode-phase P99 latency jumped ~2.1x, prefill unchanged. Looking at batching traces now. :frowning:

jia: Ugh. Any obvious signal in the profiler?

mike: Quick dump from the trace:
```
time: 2026-03-18T14:05:10Z
request_id: r-9f2b
phase: decode
kernel: matmul_v2
prefill_kv_warm: true
batch_formation_ms: 12
observed_batch_sz: 1-3 (many singletons)
p99_decode: 420ms -> 900ms
kv_cache_hit: 78% (but priming bursts show warm misses)
```

sara: Interesting that batch sizes collapsed. Could be queue policy race w/ KV priming spikes.

jia: Is this only on the new kernel selector? Any baseline numbers from v2?

mike: v2 had p99_decode ~420ms on same load. Canary shows the selector prefers smaller kernels for short sequences which seems to push small jobs into a different queue that isn't getting batched well.

ev an: @mike can you paste the token_budget & queue_policy snippets from the canary config?

mike: Sure — minimal config (sanitized):
```
"batching": {
  "target_ms": 10,
  "max_batch_tokens": 4096,
  "token_budget": {
    "initgen": 40,
    "decode": 20
  },
  "queue_policy": "phase_aware"
}
```

jia: decode token_budget 20 looks low if many requests hit KV priming. They spend cycles waiting for KV warmup and then can't form batches.

sara: Two quick experiments: 1) bump decode token_budget -> 48 and lower initgen, 2) split decode into its own fast-path queue with relaxed formation window (target_ms -> 20) so it can pool more singletons into one batch.

ev an: Could also try extending KV priming window so subsequent items see hits. Right now kv_priming_grace = 50ms which might be too short with the new selector-induced split.

mike: Run plan: A) revert selector affinity for short sequences (quick rollback) B) run experiment A: token_budget decode->48 + queue target 20ms C) telemetry: track observed_batch_sz histogram, p95/p99 decode, kv hit latency.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary kernel-selector v3 deployed by ci/cd at 2026-03-18T14:03:00Z (build b-1345).

jia: Good catch on the deploy timing — that matches the onset. If we can't revert fast, let's try the token_budget bump as a live heuristic tweak.

sara: Also add a small smoothing window to the kernel selector so it doesn't flip affinity per-request; that will reduce churn between queues. Even a 5-request sticky affinity should help.

ev an: For metrics, add a per-queue batch formation latency graph and a kv priming miss rate. Right now we only see aggregate batch size which hides queue divergence.

mike: Will patch a canary config and run. Command I used for telemetry: `./tools/trace_agg --req r-9f2b --span decode --export csv`

jia: If the decode batch size histogram shifts right after the change, we'll know it's batching starvation. If not, it's probably kernel runtime variance or heat on the GPU.

sara: On regression root cause hypothesis: kernel-selector introduced micro-affinities that route small-sequence decodes into an under-provisioned decode queue; KV priming increases per-request token cost so target_ms 10 is too aggressive and prevents grouping.

ev an: Another mitigation: when kv_cache_hit rate drops below X%, temporarily increase decode target_ms by 2x and relax token_budget. Acting as an auto-scaler for microbatches.

mike: Agreed. I'll push a canary with token_budget decode=48, target_ms=20, sticky_affinity=5 and kv_priming_grace=120ms. Observability flags on. Will post results in ~5m.

ops-bot: perf-bot: canary telemetry started (canary-id c-782).

jia: Thanks — let us know the histograms. /cc @evan for dashboard tweaks.

sara: If this fixes it, follow-up task to add a phase-aware backoff that adapts to kv priming pressure. Might be better than hard-coded budgets. :+1:

mike: Early results — batch size median jumped from 2 -> 6, p99 decode dropped to ~480ms. kv priming misses still show short bursts but overall hit-latency improved. Will keep running for an hour.

ev an: Nice. If stable, promote change to pre-prod and add an A/B to measure cost impact (larger batches may reduce per-token GPU overhead).

mike: Yep. Opening follow-up issue with notes, config diffs, and the perf dumps.

jia: Great. Thanks for the quick loop.

sara: small TODOs: 1) add per-queue histograms 2) sticky affinity 3) auto-adjust token_budget on kv miss spikes

mike: Will create PRs for 1 & 2, and a spec doc for 3.

ops-bot: incident-bot: no incident declared — monitoring only.
